lead.title: A Modigliani offered above USD 100 million, in a city on edge: Art Basel Paris opens behind anti-ram barriers and the money still arrives
lead.standfirst: Over the weekend of 17 and 18 October, student protests in France were joined by masked gangs, yet the fair's top clients still came, and the sales were large.
lead.body: Art Basel Paris opened its fifth edition at the Grand Palais this week in conditions few organisers would choose. Over 17 and 18 October, large parts of France saw disorder after student protests were joined by masked gangs, with looting concentrated around Bastille and République rather than near the fair. The Art Newspaper reports that anti-ram barriers were set up around the Grand Palais, extra guards and dogs patrolled the perimeter, and the fair said it would follow the advice of the Préfet de Paris and could close if required. Police sirens, the paper adds, sounded throughout the city. The trading nonetheless held. Artnet reports that Pace Di Donna Schrader Galleries is offering Amedeo Modigliani's Nu étendu (Lolotte) (1917) for a price in excess of USD 100 million, from the family of the collector who bought it in 1920. The Art Newspaper lists further sales at the invitation-only Avant Première on 20 October: a Gerhard Richter, Rococo Table (1965), at USD 10.5 million with Hauser & Wirth, a Julie Mehretu at USD 7.8 million with White Cube, and a George Condo at USD 2.2 million with Sprüth Magers. Artnet adds a Joan Mitchell at USD 14.5 million and a 1982 Basquiat at USD 11 million with Van de Weghe. The fair has 211 exhibitors, runs to Sunday 25 October, and public admission starts on Friday. The pattern is instructive. Andreas Gegner of Sprüth Magers told The Art Newspaper that many collectors had already booked and decided to come anyway, and the first preview day was designed to give top clients an earlier, quieter entry. Art Basel did not publish daily attendance figures. Collectors named as present included Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo, Christian Boros and Uli Sigg. Not everything moved: a small Turner watercolour priced at USD 380,000 had not sold by the second day. For the people who run a collector's travel, the week is a case study in layered contingency. Hotels, drivers, private entrances, preview slots and a decision on whether the principal travels at all were all being revised by the hour, usually before the family asked.
lead.why: A principal's decision to attend, stay away or watch from a distance rests on the quality of the security picture her household can assemble overnight, and that picture is the concierge's work product.

articles.title: Family offices want more private equity, and one in five expects its chief executive to leave within three years
articles.body: Bank of America Private Bank's 2026 Family Office Study, titled Building for Generations, surveyed 355 United States family office decision-makers in January and February, plus nine qualitative interviews. The offices range from USD 25 million to more than USD 5 billion in assets, most above USD 500 million. Private equity is cited as one of today's biggest wealth-creation opportunities by 51 per cent, the highest of any category, and 59 per cent plan to increase their exposure over the next one to three years. Alternatives already make up 37.7 per cent of the average portfolio, with private equity at 27.2 per cent of the alternatives sleeve, private real estate at 18.6 per cent and venture capital at 16.2 per cent. Illiquid assets are 44.8 per cent of the whole. Of that alternatives exposure, 59.4 per cent is held through funds and 40.6 per cent directly. Capital growth is the priority for 58 per cent of offices, against 22 per cent for a balanced approach and 20 per cent for income. The study is also a portrait of how these households work. Some 86 per cent say relationships with other family offices matter for finding investments, and 67 per cent say other family offices often have better opportunities than private equity firms. Where a next-generation principal is expected, 79 per cent anticipate alternatives taking a larger share after the transition. And 21 per cent expect their office's chief executive to depart within three years, a continuity question that sits beside the talent pressures reported across the sector this month. For the household, a portfolio that is nearly half illiquid is a household that cannot be sold down quickly. It favours steady, planned spending, and it raises the value of the staff who keep the family's operating life calm while capital is committed for a decade.
articles.why: An office whose chief executive may leave and whose capital is locked in funds leans harder on the trusted generalist who holds the family's day-to-day operations together.
articles.src: Alternatives Watch, citing the Bank of America Family Office Study

articles.title: Monaco Yacht Show closes with 118 superyachts worth EUR 4.5 billion, and a 111-metre debut
articles.body: The 35th Monaco Yacht Show ran from 23 to 26 September at Port Hercule. Organisers report 30,678 visitors, 560 exhibitors and 118 superyachts, 50 of them delivered in 2026, with an estimated combined value of EUR 4.5 billion. Oceanco's 111-metre Leviathan made her Monaco debut, and Lürssen's 102.4-metre Nixie had her world premiere. Toby Moore, chief executive of Informa Prestige, described the show as a marketplace for yacht projects rather than a parade. The report published no sales volume, deal count or contract value, so the figures describe supply and attendance, not demand. The Monaco Yacht Summit and the second Blue Wake Awards ran in parallel. The calendar ahead is worth noting. The Future of Refit is set for 31 March to 2 April 2027, the 36th Monaco Yacht Show for 22 to 25 September 2027, and an inaugural Red Sea Yacht Show for 14 to 17 October 2027 at Jeddah Yacht Club and Marina. The show also fits a wider picture. Yesterday's edition reported superyacht brokerage value down 4.7 per cent over nine months while charter bookings rose 18.5 per cent. A fleet of 118 vessels in one harbour, half a dozen of them over 100 metres, is the supply side of that same market.
articles.why: The yacht is a floating household with its own captain, purser and chief stewardess, and the shows are where the families' shore teams learn what is coming into service and which crews will be hiring.

articles.title: Prime property rose 2.6 per cent worldwide, but Tokyo gained 50.7 per cent and Dubai 10.9 per cent
articles.body:
Knight Frank's Prime Global Cities Index for the second quarter of 2026 shows prime prices up 2.6 per cent over twelve months, against 2.0 per cent in the first quarter and 3.0 per cent a year earlier. Thirty-two of 47 cities recorded positive annual growth. Liam Bailey, the firm's global head of research, calls the results a modest improvement in global luxury housing conditions, and describes performance as highly differentiated.

The leaders are Tokyo at 50.7 per cent, Manila at 14.6 per cent, Dubai at 10.9 per cent, Singapore at 9.5 per cent and Nairobi at 8.5 per cent. At the other end sit Beijing at minus 8.4 per cent, Toronto at minus 7.3 per cent, Wellington at minus 5.4 per cent, Shanghai at minus 4.9 per cent and Auckland at minus 3.8 per cent. Local supply, currency, wealth creation and interest rates shape each city's result, Bailey notes.

The spread matters because wealthy families rarely hold one address. Earlier this week Henley's view of families assembling several residences and passports was reported here, and the price table shows where those residences are increasingly being added. Each is a property to open, staff, insure, stock and secure.
articles.why: Every new address in Tokyo or Dubai is a new household to stand up, with its own staffing market, regulations and seasonal rhythm, and someone must run it.
articles.src: Knight Frank, Prime Global Cities Index Q2 2026

briefs.t: Family offices put USD 68.3 billion into deals in the third quarter, and a seventh of them were wealth manager acquisitions
briefs.b: FINTRX counted 342 company transactions between July and September, with 161 family offices investing in 319 companies, and 49 of the deals were acquisitions of registered investment advisers. In property, Pontegadea paid USD 912 million for Capital 8 in London and Ofer Global paid USD 382 million for 120 Park Avenue in New York.

briefs.t: Two former J.P. Morgan advisers launch an independent firm for ultra-wealthy families with USD 18.6 billion
briefs.b: Latigo Peak Partners announced its launch on 19 October with 48 professionals, headquartered in Palm Beach Gardens, with hubs in Bellevue and Boston. It is founder-owned, with custody at Charles Schwab and BNY Pershing.

briefs.t: Jeddah will host an inaugural Red Sea Yacht Show in October 2027
briefs.b: Organisers have announced the show for 14 to 17 October 2027 at Jeddah Yacht Club and Marina.
